requirements: docs/21 resource quotas and emergency stop
scenarios: the stop lands while a check the agent started is running: the process is gone within seconds, the call is ToolCallCancelled, the run ends RunCancelled/TaskCancelled without another model call, the queued write never happens
StartTask on a stopped session is refused EMERGENCY_STOP
the refusal survives killing and restarting the Core: the stop is a projection of the log
kept from M2.5/M7.6: leases revoked with the reason, non-read effects refused EMERGENCY_STOP by the kernel, browser input halted by the host

ci.note: the macOS desktop-E2E job passed on rerun after the documented CAPACITY_EXHAUSTED/CORE_UNAVAILABLE timing flake; every Rust job passed first time

audit: IMPLEMENTED-PARTIAL before: the stop journaled and revoked leases and the kernel refused new effects, but a running loop kept turning (it fences on the session lease generation), a process a tool ran outlived the stop (no cancellation path to the broker in the direct runner or the engine's BrokerRunner), a cancelled process was recorded as a failure or, for test.run, as a successful call carrying a CANCELLED report, and StartTask would start a run in a stopped session.
proof: On the real Core with the real terminal broker a 600 s check is killed within seconds of the stop, the outcomes are recorded honestly, no model call follows, a new run is refused and a restarted Core refuses it too; green on macOS, Linux and Windows.
negative_proof: The same test against the code before the change: the check kept running after the stop (the first local run of this task), and the call was recorded a success with a CANCELLED report.
limitations: A stop is per session and is not lifted (docs/23 names no lifting); external operations already accepted by a remote are recorded UnknownOutcome for reconciliation, not recalled; cloud-isolated process cancellation follows the guest protocol and is not separately measured here.
